This environmental interaction does not break the Ising symmetry on average (since dephasing in the z-basis preserves diagonal density matrix elements), but it does decohere off-diagonal elements of the density matrix in the z-basis, gradually suppressing transverse coherence. The experimentalist observes that: (i) at very weak transverse fields, the steady-state expectation value of the longitudinal magnetization is nearly as large as in the isolated case; (ii) at strong transverse fields, the steady state is indistinguishable from the isolated paramagnet; (iii) near the isolated system's critical point, dephasing dramatically suppresses fluctuations and broadens the susceptibility peak into a wide crossover.
